summary: W. S. Karunatillake worked in linguistics, Indology, and Buddhist studies. He was a professor at the University of Kelaniya (~1976–2004) and served as Visiting Numata Professor of Buddhist Studies at Harvard University in 1998.

Wai-lun Tam works in religious studies, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at McMaster University (~1990–1996) under Koichi Shinohara, also studying under Gérard Vallée, and became professor and department chairperson at The Chinese University of Hong Kong (~1996).

Walpola Rahula was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Ceylon (~1938–1950) under George Peiris Malalasekera, the University of Calcutta, and the University of Paris (~1950–1955) under Paul Demiéville. He later held a post at the University of Oxford.

Walter Eugene Clark, a scholar of Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies, studied at Harvard University (~1899–1906). He held posts at the University of Chicago (1923–1927) and at Harvard University, where he succeeded Charles Rockwell Lanman as Wales Professor of Sanskrit (1939).
Walter Ewer worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Fort William College in 1803 and served in the Indian Civil Service from around 1803 to 1840.

Walter Liebenthal was a scholar in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Indology. He held posts at the University of Paris, Visva-Bharati University as a visiting professor (~1952–1959), and the University of Tübingen (~1965).

Walter M. Spink worked in history, archaeology, Indology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Amherst College (~1945–1949) and held academic posts at Brandeis University (~1956–1961) and the University of Michigan (~1961–2000), where he was a professor.

Walter Simon specialized in Sinology, Tibetology, and linguistics. He studied at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1913–1921) under Otto Franke (~1920–1923), later serving there as extraordinary professor (1926–1934) before teaching at SOAS and the University of London (~1938–1960).
Walter Slaje is an Indologist who studied at the University of Vienna (~1974–1983). He later served as Prof. Dr at the University of Halle-Wittenberg from approximately 1999 to 2020.

Walter Yeeling Evans-Wentz was a scholar of religious studies, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Stanford University (~1902–1907), the University of Oxford (1907), and Jesus College (~1907–1910), also studying under Kazi Dawa Samdup (~1919–1922).
Walther Schubring was an Indologist who studied as a disciple of Ernst Leumann (~1901–1904). He held a professorship at the University of Hamburg from around 1920 to 1950.

Walther Wüst was an Indologist, linguist, and Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar. He studied at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (~1919–1923), where he later served as rector from 1941 to 1946.

Wang Pachow worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Sinology. He studied under Yun-shan Tan (~1939–1941) and served on the teaching and research staff at Visva-Bharati University from around 1941 to 1953.

Wannaporn Rienjang works in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies, earning a PhD at the University of Cambridge (~2011–2017). She held posts at the British Museum (~2012–2014), the University of Oxford (~2016–2020), and Thammasat University (~2018).
Warren Cowgill worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Stanford University (~1948–1952) and Yale University (~1952–1957), and held a post at Yale University in 1956.

Warren Lee Todd is a scholar of philosophy and Indology who completed his PhD at Lancaster University (~2008–2012) under doctoral supervisor Chakravarthi Ram-Prasad. He also studied under Irina Kuznetsova, Peter Harvey, and Chogye Trichen Rinpoche.

Warrin Ratanamalai is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned an MA at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University until 2007. There, studies were supervised by Phra Suthithammanuwat and Phra Srisitthimuni, alongside teachers including Phra Sudhivorayan and Phramaha Somjin Sammāpañño.

Wasu Harada studied Buddhist studies and Indology at Ryukoku University and Koyasan University, supervised by Eshō Mikogami, Hiroo Kashiwagi, and Makio Takemura. Harada held posts at Koyasan University, Ryukoku University, Shuchiin University, and Kyushu Ryukoku Junior College.

Wataru S. Ryose is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned a Ph.D. at the University of Wisconsin-Madison by 1987 under Minoru Kiyota, having also studied under Genjun Sasaki and Frances A. Wilson.

Wayne Proudfoot is a scholar of philosophy and religious studies who studied at Harvard Divinity School (~1963–1966) and Harvard University (~1964–1972). He took up a post at Columbia University around 1972.
